articles.title: Evolution Equity Partners Names John Cordo As Partner Following $1.1 Billion Capital Raise
articles.snippet:
Evolution Equity Partners has named John Cordo as a Partner, expanding the cybersecurity-focused investment firm's senior team following a $1.1 billion capital raise.
The post Evolution Equity Partners Names John Cordo As Partner Following $1.1 Billion Capital Raise appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Evolution Equity Partners Names John Cordo As Partner Following $1.1 Billion Capital Raise
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Evolution Equity Partners Names John Cordo As Partner Following $1.1 Billion Capital Raise
Evolution Equity Partners has named John Cordo as a Partner, expanding the cybersecurity-focused investment firm’s senior team following a $1.1 billion capital raise.
Cordo brings nearly 15 years of cybersecurity investment experience and has worked with Evolution Equity Partners for approximately three years.
He began his investment career at Blackstone, where he invested through the Blackstone Innovations venture capital portfolio.
Cordo’s cybersecurity investment experience includes companies such as HUMAN, BigID and Immuta, along with several businesses that were subsequently acquired by major technology companies.
Those investments include CloudGenix, which was acquired by Palo Alto Networks; CloudKnox, which was acquired by Microsoft; and Respond Software, which was acquired by FireEye.
Evolution Equity Partners invests in cybersecurity and related technology businesses and has been expanding its capital base and investment team as demand for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence infrastructure grows.
KEY QUOTES:
“Evolution completed a $1.1 billion capital raise expanding our capital base, team, and access to best-of-breed cybersecurity software companies amidst growing investment opportunities. We are thrilled to welcome John Cordo to the Evolution partnership.”
Richard Seewald, Founder and Managing Partner of Evolution Equity Partners
“Evolution Equity Partners is a differentiated firm due to its cyber-dedicated investors, operators, entrepreneurs, and technologists. It has been great working with the team for the past three years. I look forward to seeing what we can achieve together, especially as the cybersecurity and AI markets continue to grow at a pace we’ve never seen before.”
John Cordo, Partner at Evolution Equity Partners

articles.title: Lambda Closes $1.008 Billion Senior Secured Financing To Fund AI Infrastructure
articles.snippet:
Lambda closed a $1.008 billion investment-grade delayed-draw term loan to finance GPU infrastructure supporting committed AI infrastructure deployments. The financing represents Lambda's first U.S. fixed-rate financing and its first institutional debt transaction exceeding $1 billion.
The post Lambda Closes $1.008 Billion Senior Secured Financing To Fund AI Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lambda Closes $1.008 Billion Senior Secured Financing To Fund AI Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Lambda Closes $1.008 Billion Senior Secured Financing To Fund AI Infrastructure
Lambda closed a $1.008 billion investment-grade delayed-draw term loan to finance GPU infrastructure supporting committed AI infrastructure deployments. The financing represents Lambda’s first U.S. fixed-rate financing and its first institutional debt transaction exceeding $1 billion.
The facility was marketed to insurance companies and fixed-income investors and was oversubscribed.
Morningstar DBRS assigned the financing an A (low) rating, while Moody’s assigned a Baa1 rating.
The facility carries a fixed interest rate of 6.78% and matures on May 30, 2033.
Lambda plans to use the proceeds to purchase and develop GPU infrastructure supporting three committed customer deployments with two investment-grade offtakers across multiple data centers.
The loan is secured by the GPU servers and related infrastructure financed through the facility along with contracted cash flows.
The delayed-draw structure aligns capital deployment with cluster commissioning milestones.
The transaction follows Lambda’s broadly syndicated loan financing completed in August 2026.
Lambda said its major 2026 financings have each raised approximately $1 billion, demonstrating its growing access to institutional credit markets.
Support: J.P. Morgan served as sole coordinating lead arranger, structuring agent, and bookrunner. Davis Polk & Wardwell advised Lambda, while Latham & Watkins represented the lenders.
KEY QUOTES:
“The capital in this offering underwrites infrastructure in decades, not quarters, and has funded us as a private company on the strength of our customer contracts.”
“Our progression into deeper and more diversified pools of capital is the market’s verdict on the durability of our contracts and scalability of our business.”
Michel Combes, CEO of Lambda

articles.title: Exclusive: Daytona, a startup building the ‘agentic cloud,’ valued at $1 billion in latest funding round
articles.snippet: Exclusive: Daytona, a startup building the ‘agentic cloud,’ valued at $1 billion in latest funding round Fortune
articles.text:
AI agents need somewhere to work—and Ivan Burazin thinks the existing cloud providers aren’t the right answer. Now Burazin, the cofounder and CEO of Daytona, a San Francisco-based startup, has turned the idea of a new kind of cloud just for AI agents into a unicorn business.
Recommended Video
Daytona said Tuesday it has raised a $60 million Series B venture capital round at a $1 billion valuation. FirstMark led the round. It was joined by an A-list roster of Silicon Valley founders, including Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo and Zoom’s Eric Yuan, plus strategic investors Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next and Okta Ventures.
Burazin told Fortune that about $50 million of the round came from existing investors. The new funding brings the amount Daytona has raised to date to about $91 million.
Why agents need their own computers
An AI agent that writes and runs code, browses the web or operates business software needs to use a computer—either an actual machine, or a virtual one, running in the cloud. For many use cases, having a virtual machine is preferable—it allows the AI agent to operate even if the person running the agent shuts down their laptop, and because virtual machines can be configured with only the software and network access the agent needs to do a particular task and nothing more, it is generally a safer way to run AI agents. A virtual machine, or “sandbox” as they are sometimes called, minimizes the chance that the agent will run amok and take damaging unauthorized actions, or that an outside party could hijack the agent and get it to divulge sensitive data.
Daytona was founded in 2023 by Burazin, Goran Draganić and Vedran Jukić to automate software development environments for large enterprises. When the founders saw that agents would need computers too, Burazin said, they “basically gave our competitors all our customers, rebuilt everything, had like three months left of revenue in the bank, and then relaunched this thing.”
Daytona currently provides these sandboxes to many of the leading AI companies, which use the virtual machines to allow their models to practice tasks over and over inside sandboxes during training and testing. Daytona says AI data company Snorkel, which also helps customers test and benchmark AI models, has provisioned more than one million sandboxes on its platform. It also counts Anthropic, OpenAI, Nvidia , Cursor, Cognition, Meta and Cohere among its customers.
Burazin said that Daytona’s revenue run rate grew 25-fold between January and September. “We’ve been growing on average every single month 50.9%,” Burazin said.
Existing cloud providers, such as Amazon’s AWS, Microsoft’s Azure, or Google’s Google Cloud Platform, allow customers to spin up virtual machines. But doing so takes between 30 seconds and many minutes, depending on the complexity of the configuration. This, Burazin said, is far too long for the future of agentic work, when companies may be deploying thousands or even tens of thousands of AI agents, each of which may need access to different software tools depending on the task they are being asked to complete.
Daytona can configure a new sandbox for an AI agent in 60 milliseconds, according to Burazin. That is roughly half the time it takes to blink. The trick, he said, is to pre-distribute snapshots of configured machines onto the physical drives of servers. When an agent needs a machine, Daytona attaches processing

articles.title: Instinct Raises $1 Billion in Series C at a $10 Billion Valuation
articles.snippet: Instinct Raises $1 Billion in Series C at a $10 Billion Valuation www.tokenpost.com
articles.text:
Home Business 1 min read Add as a preferred source on Google
Instinct Raises $1 Billion in Series C at a $10 Billion Valuation
The Sept. 28 round names Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital and Coatue as investors; Instinct’s personal assistant remains in early access.
By John Kim
Published Oct 22, 2026, 6:12 AM EDT
Save Share A smartphone rests beside a paper grocery bag on an entry bench / TokenPost.ai
Instinct's Sept. 28 announcement put the $1 billion Series C at a $10 billion company valuation, four times August's $2.5 billion mark for the San Francisco startup.
The San Francisco-based company named Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital and Coatue as investors. Its August Series B raised $250 million at a $2.5 billion valuation and brought total funding to $350 million. The Series C amount is four times the size of that earlier round.
Instinct is an early-access personal assistant users can reach by text or phone. Its phone and computer let it take on tasks such as arranging trips, placing grocery orders and ending subscriptions.
Newer features include call concierge support and a Trusted Person Network, which enables Instinct assistants to coordinate. The product remains in early access.
Founder Noah Shinn said, “This funding helps us bring Instinct to more people and continue building the future of personal AI.”
John Kim

articles.snippet:
Blackstone Credit & Insurance led a $1 billion financing to support the combination of Analogic Corporation with the Security Enterprise Solutions, Ports & Borders, and Industrial Automation businesses of Leidos Holdings.
The post Blackstone Credit & Insurance Leads $1 Billion Financing For Analogic And Leidos Security Businesses Combination appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blackstone Credit & Insurance Leads $1 Billion Financing For Analogic And Leidos Security Businesses Combination
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Blackstone Credit & Insurance Leads $1 Billion Financing For Analogic And Leidos Security Businesses Combination
Blackstone Credit & Insurance led a $1 billion financing to support the combination of Analogic Corporation with the Security Enterprise Solutions, Ports & Borders, and Industrial Automation businesses of Leidos Holdings.
The transaction brings together Analogic with the Leidos businesses to create a larger global security imaging and detection company serving airports, ports, borders, critical infrastructure, and other mission-critical environments.
The combination closed earlier in October 2026.
Blackstone Credit & Insurance served as lead lender and joint lead arranger on the financing.
HPS, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo also served as joint lead arrangers.
The combined company brings together broader security detection capabilities, expanded customer relationships, and greater operating scale.
Analogic is headquartered in Salem, New Hampshire, and provides advanced imaging, detection, automation, and power technology solutions.
Its portfolio serves aviation security, ports and borders, critical infrastructure, healthcare, and industrial markets.
Analogic combines imaging technologies, artificial intelligence, precision power, automation, and lifecycle support capabilities.
Blackstone Credit & Insurance said the financing demonstrates its ability to provide large-scale and flexible capital to established platforms.
BXCI invests across private investment grade, asset-based lending, public investment grade and high yield, infrastructure debt, direct lending, collateralized loan obligations, sustainable resources, and opportunistic credit.
Altaris, which focuses exclusively on healthcare investments, manages $10 billion of equity capital and has invested in more than 50 companies since its founding in 2003.
Leidos has approximately 50,000 employees globally and reported annual revenue of approximately $17.2 billion for the fiscal year ended January 2, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to support the combined business with this financing solution to help create a scaled, integrated leader in security detection. This transaction reflects our ability to provide large-scale, flexible capital to market-leading platforms.”
Brad Colman, Global Head of Healthcare Investing and Sponsor Coverage for Private Credit Strategies at Blackstone Credit & Insurance

articles.title: SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion
articles.snippet:
Volato Group, which is in the process of rebranding as SOAR AI, entered into a common stock purchase agreement with an institutional investor for an equity facility of up to $1 billion.
The post SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
SOAR AI Secures Up To $1 Billion Equity Facility To Support AI Infrastructure Expansion
Volato Group, which is in the process of rebranding as SOAR AI, entered into a common stock purchase agreement with an institutional investor for an equity facility of up to $1 billion.
The company said the facility is designed to support the development of its Ohio AI infrastructure campus and additional powered industrial sites it is exploring in the U.S. and internationally.
SOAR AI retains control over whether, when, and how much capital it draws from the facility and has no obligation to sell any shares.
The company’s Ohio campus currently has 154 MW of power available, with a roadmap to increase capacity to 480 MW.
Proceeds from any future draws are expected to support power, cooling, data center infrastructure, GPU compute deployments, and the development of additional AI infrastructure locations.
SOAR AI said its development strategy focuses on reusing existing industrial sites and electrical infrastructure where practical rather than building entirely new facilities.
The Ohio campus is the first location to use this approach, and the company is also evaluating additional brownfield and similar industrial sites domestically and internationally.
The financing follows commercial agreements announced in September 2026.
SOAR AI entered into a master services agreement and two four-year, take-or-pay orders with a large AI customer representing $1.17 billion in aggregate contract value.
Those orders include approximately $133 million in contractual customer prepayments and call for dedicated, single-tenant AMD GPU clusters.
The contractual start dates are December 31, 2026, and June 30, 2027.
The company said it is also in active discussions with additional prospective customers for available and planned AI infrastructure capacity.
SOAR AI expects the equity facility to complement customer prepayments, project-level financing, and other sources of capital as it expands.
Under the agreement, each sale is limited to 10% of average daily trading volume, with combined daily sales capped at $6 million.
Subsequent sales must be spaced at least two trading days apart and cannot occur when the prior day’s volume-weighted average price was the lowest of the preceding 10 trading days.
The investor also agreed not to sell short or hedge SOAR AI’s common stock during the term of the agreement.
The investor may not own more than 4.99% of the company’s outstanding common stock at any time.
Without stockholder approval, total issuances under the facility are capped at 19.99% of the shares outstanding on the signing date under NYSE American requirements.
No sales can begin until a resale registration statement covering the shares is filed with and declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
SOAR AI said the company can terminate the agreement without penalty on one trading day’s notice, provided no put notice is pending.
Volato Group expects its corporate name change to SOAR AI, Inc. to become effective on October 19, 2026, subject to applicable regulatory and stock exchange requirements.
The company is building an AI infrastructure platform combining data center infrastructure, high-density GPU compute, high-performance networking, and related technologies for AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing workloads.

articles.title: Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise
articles.snippet:
Omni Bridgeway closed its Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 capital raise at the full targeted size of $1 billion. The final close expands the legal finance firm’s institutional investor base while maintaining a high level of participation from existing investors.
The post Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Omni Bridgeway Closes $1 Billion Legal Finance Fundraise
Omni Bridgeway closed its Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 capital raise at the full targeted size of $1 billion. The final close expands the legal finance firm’s institutional investor base while maintaining a high level of participation from existing investors.
Investors representing 99% of Series 1 commitments reinvested in Series 2.
More than 50% of Series 2 capital was committed by repeat Series 1 investors.
The fundraising increases Omni Bridgeway’s assets under management to approximately A$5.9 billion, or $4.2 billion.
The close comes as Omni Bridgeway marks its 40th year operating as a specialist investor in legal assets and its 25th year listed on the Australian Securities Exchange.
Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 will invest across legal assets diversified by jurisdiction, area of law, and investment strategy.
Omni Bridgeway is contributing approximately 20% of the capital in Series 2 through general partner co-investment.
As of June 30, 2026, the firm had completed 822 investments across its platform.
Omni Bridgeway reported a portfolio-wide multiple of invested capital of 2.4x across multiple decades and economic cycles.
The company said its capital model is designed to provide funded parties with dedicated capital committed to individual matters.
Omni Bridgeway also emphasized that it remains the sole decision-maker on its capital commitments and that funding availability is not dependent on other portfolio outcomes, third-party underwriting, syndication, or broader capital market conditions.
The $1 billion fundraising forms part of a broader capital strategy that also includes sidecar capital and structured finance solutions.
Omni Bridgeway plans to continue scaling and diversifying its legal finance platform across jurisdictions and areas of law.
The company operates with approximately 160 professionals across more than 20 locations and 15 countries.
KEY QUOTES:
“In legal finance, institutional capital is consolidating around mature, scaled managers with proprietary origination and work-out capability, and a track record of disciplined underwriting that has performed through multiple economic cycles.”
“Our successful close, the 99% reinvestment rate, and the sophisticated institutional quality of our investment base reflect our leading position within legal finance.”
“Funded parties increasingly and rightly focus on capital availability, long-term stability and commitment authority. Every dollar we commit is matched by dedicated fund capital earmarked to that matter. Omni Bridgeway is the sole decision-maker, and the availability of our capital commitment is not exposed to the outcome of other portfolio investments, capital market conditions, third-party underwriting or syndication. Counterparties increasingly recognize and value these differentiators – and accordingly assign a premium to our capital.”
“The US$1 billion raised in connection with Funds 4 and 5 Series 2 sits alongside a broader capital strategy, with sidecar capital and structured finance solutions continuing to expand alongside our core funds, supporting Omni Bridgeway’s aim of further scaling and diversifying its platform.”
Raymond van Hulst, Managing Director and CEO of Omni Bridgeway

Hightower Signature Wealth Brings In $1 Billion Team Synergy Capital Solutions
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Hightower Signature Wealth Brings In $1 Billion Team Synergy Capital Solutions
Hightower Advisors announced that Synergy Capital Solutions has joined Hightower Signature Wealth, adding approximately $1 billion in assets under management to the platform.
Synergy is a Bloomfield Hills, Michigan-based wealth management firm serving affluent individuals across the U.S. The firm has been a Hightower partner since 2017 and will now operate as part of Hightower Signature Wealth.
The transaction closed on September 30, 2026.
Synergy brings a multigenerational team of 15 professionals, including seven advisors, to Hightower Signature Wealth. The team plans to maintain offices in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan; Naples, Florida; and Lebanon, Pennsylvania.
Synergy takes a collaborative approach to financial planning and portfolio management, working with clients to align investment and wealth management strategies with their goals, priorities, and values.
As part of Hightower Signature Wealth, Synergy will gain access to expanded investment, operational, technology, compliance, marketing, and client service capabilities.
Hightower Signature Wealth’s model combines personalized financial advice with centralized infrastructure, allowing advisors to spend more time working directly with clients while benefiting from the resources and scale of a larger wealth management organization.
Synergy was founded more than four decades ago and has developed a broad range of wealth management solutions intended to support clients through different stages of their financial lives.
The firm’s leadership includes Mark Burns, CEO, Chief Investment Officer and Co-Founder; Jordann M. Andrusiak, CFP, Advisor and Chief Operating Officer; and Eric M. Nahat, CEPA, Advisor and Co-Chief Investment Officer.
Following the Synergy transaction, Hightower Signature Wealth has approximately $40 billion in assets under management, more than 160 advisors, and over 35 locations nationwide.
Hightower said it expects to announce additional Hightower Signature Wealth acquisitions through the end of 2026.
Hightower Advisors oversees more than $350 billion in assets and provides investment management, financial planning, retirement planning, 401(k) consulting, and cash management services through its network of advisor businesses.
The broader Hightower platform is designed to serve as a growth partner for independent wealth management firms seeking additional technology, investment capabilities, operational infrastructure, and strategic resources while maintaining their client-focused advisory models.

Mark Burns, CEO, Chief Investment Officer and Co-Founder of Synergy Capital Solutions

articles.snippet:
Megaport has secured approximately A$1 billion in new AI infrastructure contracts as the network and computing company continues expanding its AI infrastructure business.

articles.text:
Megaport Secures About A$1 Billion In New AI Infrastructure Contracts And Raises FY2027 Guidance
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Megaport Secures About A$1 Billion In New AI Infrastructure Contracts And Raises FY2027 Guidance
Megaport has secured approximately A$1 billion in new AI infrastructure contracts as the network and computing company continues expanding its AI infrastructure business.
Since April, the company has announced approximately A$2.3 billion in total strategic contract value.
Combined with Megaport’s existing business, the contracts are expected to support approximately A$1.1 billion in pro forma Group annual recurring revenue once deployed.
More than 85% of pro forma ARR is expected to come from North America.
Megaport reported pro forma liquidity of A$362.2 million. Network net revenue retention reached 116%, increasing six percentage points from the prior corresponding period.
Network ARR reached A$302.6 million, representing growth of 29% from the prior corresponding period.
Compute ARR increased to A$201.4 million, representing growth of 90% since June 30, 2026, and 227% since the acquisition of the business.
Customers have committed approximately A$323 million in prepayments related to the contracts, supporting infrastructure investments required for future deployments.
The company is also broadening its customer base, replenishing its GPU pool and expanding its AI inference platform.
Megaport raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to between A$720 million and A$810 million, compared with its previous guidance of A$620 million to A$730 million.
The company also raised its expected EBITDA margin to between 42% and 44%, up from its prior range of 38% to 40%.
Planned capital expenditures were increased to between A$1.78 billion and A$1.88 billion from the previous range of A$1.28 billion to A$1.38 billion.

articles.title: OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
articles.snippet:
OpenText completed a $1 billion senior secured notes offering and amended its revolving credit facility as the enterprise software company refinances upcoming debt maturities and extends portions of its capital structure.
The post OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
OpenText Completes $1 Billion Senior Secured Notes Offering And Extends Revolving Credit Facility
OpenText completed a $1 billion senior secured notes offering and amended its revolving credit facility as the enterprise software company refinances upcoming debt maturities and extends portions of its capital structure.
The offering consists of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 6.700% senior secured notes due in 2031 and $500 million of 7.150% senior secured notes due in 2033.
By issuing debt with maturities extending into the next decade, OpenText is addressing nearer-term obligations while giving itself more time before a significant portion of the newly issued principal comes due.
The company also amended its revolving credit facility, primarily extending its maturity from December 19, 2028, to October 1, 2031, subject to the terms and conditions of the facility.
Together, the notes offering and revolving-credit amendment represent a significant refinancing initiative designed to reduce OpenText’s exposure to upcoming maturities in 2027 and 2028.
OpenText plans to use the net proceeds from the offering, together with cash on hand, primarily to redeem its entire $1 billion principal amount of 6.900% senior secured notes due in 2027.
The planned redemption includes the applicable premium, accrued and unpaid interest and other costs and expenses associated with retiring the securities.
Replacing the 2027 notes with debt maturing in 2031 and 2033 substantially extends the company’s repayment timetable.
The new notes carry coupons of 6.700% and 7.150%, compared with 6.900% on the securities being redeemed.
Because the new financing is divided evenly between the two tranches, OpenText has created a more staggered maturity structure rather than replacing the entire $1 billion obligation with another single maturity.
That can help reduce refinancing concentration by spreading future principal requirements across separate years.
OpenText also intends to use available proceeds to purchase up to $300 million in principal amount of its outstanding 3.875% senior notes due in 2028 through an existing tender offer.
The company expected to redeem the 2027 notes and settle the tender offer on October 2, 2026.
If the company purchases the full $300 million targeted under the tender offer, the transaction would further reduce the amount of debt approaching maturity over the next two years.
The refinancing therefore addresses both OpenText’s 2027 secured notes and a portion of its 2028 senior notes.
The strategy gives the company greater visibility into its debt obligations while shifting more of its capital structure toward maturities beginning in 2031.
OpenText’s amended revolving credit facility similarly pushes an important source of liquidity further out.
A revolving credit facility provides companies with flexible access to capital that can be borrowed, repaid and drawn again subject to the facility’s terms.
Extending its maturity through October 2031 reduces the risk that OpenText would need to renegotiate or replace the facility during the same period in which other debt obligations were approaching maturity.
The amendment can therefore provide additional financial flexibility alongside the new notes.
The newly issued securities are senior secured obligations.
They are guaranteed on a senior secured basis by OpenT
